claim: Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 lists Equifax Workforce Solutions LLC (Missouri) as a subsidiary; the 10-K describes The Work Number, run by its Workforce Solutions segment, as built on payroll data from over 4 million organizations.

Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 lists Appriss Insights, LLC as a subsidiary of Equifax Inc. as of December 31, 2025; the 10-K says proceeds of its August 2021 issue of 2.35% Senior Notes due 2031 helped fund acquisitions, including the Company's acquisition of Appriss Insights.
Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 lists IXI Corporation as a subsidiary of Equifax Inc. as of December 31, 2025.
Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 lists Teletrack, LLC as a subsidiary of Equifax Inc. as of December 31, 2025.
Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 lists DataX, Ltd. as a subsidiary of Equifax Inc. as of December 31, 2025.
Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 lists Kount Inc. as a subsidiary of Equifax Inc. as of December 31, 2025.
Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K says its U.S. mortgage solutions include tri-merge credit reports that combine information from Equifax, Experian and TransUnion into a single report.
Equifax's FY2025 Form 10-K says its U.S. mortgage solutions include tri-merge credit reports that combine information from Equifax, Experian and TransUnion into a single report.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K refers to its acquisition of Neustar in December 2021, and Exhibit 21 lists Neustar, Inc. and several Neustar data entities as subsidiaries.

TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K lists TLOxp among its own products: its TruLookup investigative solution line "includes TLOxp® as a platform for delivery." TLOxp is a TransUnion product platform, not a separately listed legal entity.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K refers to its acquisition of Argus, and Exhibit 21 lists Argus Information and Advisory Services, Inc. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists Tru Optik Data Corp. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists iovation Inc. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists FactorTrust, Inc. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists LSSi Data Corp. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists Signal Digital, Inc. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists TransUnion Rental Screening Solutions, Inc. as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists Drivers History Information Sales LLC as a subsidiary.
TransUnion's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 lists TransUnion Risk and Alternative Data Solutions, Inc. as a subsidiary.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Experian Information Solutions, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Experian Marketing Solutions, LLC (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Tapad, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Predictive Pop, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026; the report identifies Predictive Pop, Inc. as Audigent.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Clarity Services, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Experian Background Data, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists The 41st Parameter, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 lists Neuro-ID, Inc. (USA) among its subsidiary undertakings at 31 March 2026.
Experian plc's Annual Report 2026 says it acquired US-based data and email intelligence company AtData, LLC on 18 February 2026 for US$225m, adding over 10 billion email addresses to its data assets.

RELX's Annual Report 2025 (note 28, Related undertakings) lists LexisNexis Risk Solutions Inc. (USA) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.
RELX's Annual Report 2025 (note 28, Related undertakings) lists ID Analytics, LLC (USA) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.

RELX's Annual Report 2025 (note 28, Related undertakings) lists LexisNexis Risk Data Management, LLC (USA) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.

RELX's Annual Report 2025 (note 28, Related undertakings) lists LexisNexis Special Services Inc. (USA) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.

RELX's Annual Report 2025 (note 28, Related undertakings) lists LexisNexis Coplogic Solutions Inc. (USA) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.
RELX's Annual Report 2025 (note 28, Related undertakings) lists LNRS Data Services Inc. (USA) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.

RELX's Annual Report 2025 says its LexisNexis Risk Solutions business closed the acquisition of IDVerse, a provider of AI-powered automated document authentication and fraud detection, in Q1 2025; note 28 lists IDVerse Pty Ltd (Australia) as an undertaking held indirectly by RELX PLC, at a 100% effective interest unless stated otherwise.

Verisk's FY2025 Form 10-K discloses putative class actions against Hyundai Motor America and Verisk alleging that driving data collected through vehicle software was transmitted to Verisk and shared with auto insurers; these are plaintiffs' allegations, and the 10-K describes the suits as dismissed to date (its wording does not make clear whether that covers every suit).

Omnicom's FY2025 Form 10-K says Omnicom completed its merger with The Interpublic Group (IPG) on November 26, 2025, that Acxiom was acquired from IPG, and Exhibit 21 lists Acxiom, LLC as a significant 100%-owned subsidiary.

Publicis Groupe's Universal Registration Document 2025 (Note 36) lists Epsilon Data Management LLC (United States) as a main consolidated company with 100% control and interest at December 31, 2025, and section 1.3 says Publicis acquired Epsilon, "a technology company specializing in data and marketing activities", in 2019.
Publicis Groupe's Universal Registration Document 2025 (Note 36) lists Conversant LLC (United States) as a main consolidated company with 100% control and interest at December 31, 2025.

Publicis Groupe's Universal Registration Document 2025 (Note 3) says it acquired 100% of Lotame Solutions, Inc., a specialist in data and digital identity solutions, in April 2025 for €122 million cash consideration; Note 36 lists it at 100% control.
Dun & Bradstreet's FY2024 Form 10-K says it acquired NetWise Data, LLC in 2021 to expand its Data Cloud.
Dun & Bradstreet's FY2024 Form 10-K says it acquired Eyeota Holdings Pte. Ltd. in 2021 to expand its Data Cloud.

The FTC's July 2024 second amended complaint in FTC v. Kochava alleges Collective Data Solutions, LLC is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kochava to which Kochava transferred at least part of its data broker business around July 2023.

The FTC's April 2024 complaint against X-Mode Social and Outlogic states that, in a May 2021 joint venture, X-Mode transferred its business to successor Outlogic, which became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Digital Envoy.
The FTC's 2024 complaint against Gravy Analytics and Venntel (FTC File No. 212-3035) states Venntel is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Gravy Analytics.

The FTC alleged in its 2024 complaint against Gravy Analytics and Venntel (FTC File No. 212-3035) that Gravy Analytics transfers location data to its subsidiary Venntel, which sells it to public sector customers such as government contractors.
The FTC's January 2026 complaint (Docket C-4828) states OnStar, LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of General Motors Company.

The FTC alleged in its January 2026 complaint (Docket C-4828) that GM and OnStar furnished OnStar Smart Driver enrollees' identifying information and driving data to consumer reporting agency Insurance Services Office, Inc. d/b/a Verisk Analytics under a 2016 Telematics Data Exchange Program, ending March 2024; GM settled without admitting the allegations.

The FTC alleged in its January 2026 complaint (Docket C-4828) that GM and OnStar sold driving event data, including precise geolocation, from OnStar Smart Driver enrollees to consumer reporting agency LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Inc. under an August 2019 contract, ending March 2024; GM settled without admitting the allegations.

The FTC alleged in its January 2026 complaint (Docket C-4828) that GM and OnStar licensed connected-vehicle precise geolocation data to Wejo Ltd. from 2018 until Wejo's bankruptcy, with Wejo permitted to sublicense to GM-approved 'egress licensees'.

The FTC alleged in its January 2026 complaint (Docket C-4828) that GM and OnStar licensed connected-vehicle location data to Jacobs Engineering Group, which acquired Wejo's assets on January 3, 2024, and continued sharing Smart Driver data with Jacobs until April 5, 2024.
The FTC's 2024 complaint against Avast states Jumpshot, Inc. was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Avast Ltd until Jumpshot's operations closed in January 2020.

The FTC alleged in its 2024 complaint that from 2014 through January 2020 Avast transferred browsing information collected by its software to subsidiary Jumpshot, which sold it; Avast settled without admitting the allegations.
The FTC alleged in its 2024 Avast complaint that from May 2017 to April 2019 Jumpshot granted LiveRamp a world-wide license to use granular browsing information, including for data-driven marketing.

The FTC alleged in its 2024 Avast complaint that an agreement between LiveRamp and Jumpshot provided for "ID Syncing Services", a "synchronization and matching of identifiers" between the two companies.

The FTC alleged in its 2024 Avast complaint that an August 2018 contract let Lotame match, combine and model Jumpshot's data with Lotame's and license the modeled data to Lotame customers, with revenue shared with Jumpshot.

The FTC alleged in its 2024 Avast complaint that under a December 2017 contract Jumpshot agreed to provide Omnicom an 'All Clicks Feed' for 50% of its user base in six countries, at roughly $2 million per year in the first work order.

The FTC alleged in its 2024 Avast complaint that Jumpshot's December 2017 contract with Omnicom allowed Omnicom to "map out/translate Jumpshot GUIDs into" Neustar IDs and to match with LiveRamp; the complaint does not say whether Omnicom did so.
The FTC's 2023 complaint against Instant Checkmate and TruthFinder states PubRec, LLC has wholly owned TruthFinder since 2018.
The FTC's 2023 complaint against Instant Checkmate and TruthFinder states PubRec, LLC has wholly owned Instant Checkmate since 2018.
The CFPB/FTC October 2023 complaint states TransUnion Rental Screening Solutions, Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of Trans Union LLC.

The CFPB/FTC October 2023 complaint alleges TransUnion Rental Screening Solutions purchases the information in its eviction proceeding records from third-party vendor LexisNexis Risk and Information Analytics Group, Inc.; the case settled by stipulated order, in which the defendants neither admit nor deny the allegations.

The FTC alleged in its December 2014 complaint that the defendants, Sitesearch Corporation d/b/a LeapLab, LeapLab, LLC, Leads Company, LLC and John Ayers, sold consumer payday loan applications or information assembled from them to Ideal Financial Solutions, knowing or having reason to know Ideal used it for unauthorized debits.

The FTC alleged in its August 2015 complaint that the defendants, Sequoia One, LLC, Gen X Marketing Group, LLC and individual defendants Jason A. Kotzker, Theresa D. Bartholomew, John E. Bartholomew, Jr. and Paul T. McDonnell, sold sensitive information from payday loan applications to Ideal Financial Solutions, a non-lender.

The DOJ/FTC February 2023 complaint against GoodRx alleges GoodRx shared users' medication and health information with Facebook, including uploading lists of users who bought particular medications for ad targeting.
The DOJ/FTC February 2023 complaint against GoodRx alleges GoodRx configured a Google pixel and SDK to share users' medication information, contact details and advertising IDs with Google.
The DOJ/FTC February 2023 complaint against GoodRx alleges GoodRx shared user health information, including GoodRx Coupons accessed or used, with Criteo.
The DOJ/FTC February 2023 complaint against GoodRx alleges GoodRx shared sensitive user information with third parties including Twilio.
ChexSystems' website (accessed 2026-10-18) states that 'Chex Systems, Inc. is a consumer reporting agency and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of FIS.'
Data Axle's Privacy Policy (accessed 2026-10-18) lists Consumer Base LLC dba Exact Data among the affiliates and subsidiaries with which it may share data.
Data Axle's Privacy Policy (accessed 2026-10-18) lists DonorBase, Inc. among the affiliates and subsidiaries with which it may share data.
Data Axle's Privacy Policy (accessed 2026-10-18) lists infoUSA Inc. and infoUSA Marketing, Inc. among the affiliates and subsidiaries with which it may share data.
Data Axle's Privacy Policy (accessed 2026-10-18) lists Lake Group Media, Inc. among the affiliates and subsidiaries with which it may share data.

PeopleConnect's home page (accessed 2026-10-18) presents Intelius among the brands through which 'we are one of the largest ... sources in the people search industry', and its privacy policy lists Intelius's site as a PeopleConnect 'sister site'.

PeopleConnect's home page (accessed 2026-10-18) presents TruthFinder among the brands through which 'we are one of the largest ... sources in the people search industry', and its privacy policy lists TruthFinder's site as a PeopleConnect 'sister site'.

PeopleConnect's home page (accessed 2026-10-18) presents Instant Checkmate among the brands through which 'we are one of the largest ... sources in the people search industry', and its privacy policy lists Instant Checkmate's site as a PeopleConnect 'sister site'.
Quick People Trace's site footer (accessed 2026-10-18) gives the operator as 'QuickLocate LLC, Mechanicsville, VA'.
USATrace's site footer (accessed 2026-10-18) gives the operator as 'QuickLocate LLC, Mechanicsville, VA'.

Washington Post reporting (Dec. 2021, via Boston Globe) says the National Consumer Telecom & Utilities Exchange gave utility header data to Equifax, which Equifax said NCTUE had allowed it to license for law-enforcement purposes; NCTUE said in 2021 it was ending the practice.
Washington Post reporting (Dec. 2021, via Boston Globe) says Equifax sold NCTUE utility header data for use in databases including Thomson Reuters' CLEAR, a service ICE subscribes to.

The Markup reported in Dec. 2021 that Life360 sold location data to X-Mode, confirmed by a former Life360 employee, a former X-Mode employee, and Life360's CEO naming X-Mode among about a dozen data partners.
The Markup reported in Dec. 2021 that Cuebiq received raw location data from Life360, per former employees and Life360's CEO; Cuebiq said it provides only aggregated data to its customers.
The Markup reported in Dec. 2021 that Life360's privacy policy disclosed Arity as a data partner and that Life360 said it would continue selling precise location data only to Arity.

The Markup reported in Dec. 2021 that a former Life360 employee and a Life360 executive's email it viewed identified SafeGraph as a buyer of Life360 data; Life360's CEO declined to confirm, citing confidentiality.
Motherboard reported in Nov. 2020 that Muslim Pro was among the apps sending location data to X-Mode; Muslim Pro then said it would stop sharing data with X-Mode.

Motherboard reported in Nov. 2020 that archived versions of X-Mode's website listed Sierra Nevada Corporation as a customer; X-Mode said it does not work with Sierra Nevada but did not deny it had been a customer.

Motherboard reported in Nov. 2020 that archived versions of X-Mode's website listed Systems & Technology Research as a customer; X-Mode said it does not work with STR but did not deny it had been a customer.

Sens. Wyden and Markey wrote to the FTC on July 26, 2024 that, per information Honda gave Wyden's office, Honda shared data from 97,000 cars with Verisk between 2020 and 2024 for $25,920 (26 cents per car).

Sens. Wyden and Markey wrote to the FTC on July 26, 2024 that, per information Hyundai provided, Hyundai shared data from 1.7 million vehicles with Verisk between 2018 and 2024 for $1,043,315.69 (61 cents per car).

EFF reported in Aug. 2022, from public records, that evidence (a Venntel-headed license agreement, an Iowa DPS email Fog forwarded to Venntel, and Venntel URLs in Fog's code) suggests Venntel is the source of Fog Data Science's location data; EFF said it could not confirm this for sure.

Motherboard reported in Jan. 2019 that T-Mobile shared location data with aggregator Zumigo, which shared information with Microbilt, whose phone-tracking product was used to locate a reporter's phone for a bounty hunter.
Motherboard reported in Jan. 2021 that the developer of the Salaat First prayer app confirmed the app sent users' location data to Predicio.

Motherboard reported in Jan. 2021 that documents shared by NRK show Gravy Analytics, Venntel's parent, obtained data from Predicio; it was unclear whether Salaat First data specifically reached Gravy.
NRK reported in Dec. 2020 that Gravy Analytics' response to a data-access request named Complementics (and Predicio) as companies its data on the reporter came from.
The Markup reported in June 2023 that a May 2021 Xandr file of 650,000 marketplace audience segments listed Oracle as data supplier for more than a third of them.
The Markup reported in June 2023 that a May 2021 Xandr file of marketplace audience segments listed Acxiom among the segment data suppliers.
The Markup reported in June 2023 that a May 2021 Xandr file of marketplace audience segments listed Experian as supplier of segments such as "Tough Times".
The Markup reported in June 2023 that segments in a May 2021 Xandr marketplace file came from consumer credit agencies including Equifax.
The Markup reported in June 2023 that a May 2021 Xandr marketplace file listed Foursquare (Factual) as supplier of extensive geofenced audience segments.

Sen. Wyden's Feb. 13, 2024 letter to the FTC and SEC says Near's chief privacy officer confirmed to Wyden's staff that Near had for three years sold location data to defense contractor AELIUS Exploitation Technologies.

Sen. Wyden's Feb. 13, 2024 letter says Near's attorney told his staff that, until June 2023, location data Near sold about Americans included data from the ad exchange OpenX; the WSJ reported exchanges then cut Near off.

Sen. Wyden's Feb. 13, 2024 letter says Near's attorney told his staff that, until June 2023, location data Near sold about Americans included data from the ad exchange Smaato; the WSJ reported exchanges then cut Near off.

Sen. Wyden's Feb. 13, 2024 letter says Recrue Media's co-founder told his staff its employees used Near's website to geofence about 600 Planned Parenthood locations for the Veritas Society's anti-abortion ad campaign.
ProPublica reported in Dec. 2016 that Facebook signed a data deal with Datalogix in 2012 and that Datalogix provided about 350 types of data to Facebook.
ProPublica reported in Dec. 2016 that Acxiom was one of the data brokers supplying Facebook's broker-sourced ad-targeting categories.
